Slow Sunday Tomato Soup

By Priya Raman

MARKER_RECIPE_LEDE Every family I know has a soup that means the week is over and the slow part of the weekend can begin. Ours is this tomato soup, which is less a recipe than a ritual: tomatoes roasted until they slump, onions cooked past the point where anyone is still watching the clock, and a blender doing the rest.

I have made this soup in three apartments and one very small cabin, and it has never once complained about the kitchen. Canned tomatoes work when fresh ones are pale and mealy, which honestly is most of the year. The one thing the recipe refuses to forgive is hurrying the onions.

What follows is the version I settled into after about thirty batches. It makes enough for four generous bowls, or two bowls and tomorrow's lunch, which is the correct answer.

Prep 15 minutes · Cook 1 hour · Serves 4

Ingredients

  • 2 kg ripe tomatoes, halved (or two 800 g cans)
  • 2 large onions, sliced thin
  • 6 cloves garlic, unpeeled
  • 3 tablespoons olive oil
  • 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
  • 750 ml vegetable stock
  • Salt, black pepper, a pinch of sugar
  • MARKER_INGREDIENT a splash of cream to finish, optional

Method

  1. Roast the tomatoes and garlic at 180°C for forty minutes, until the edges char and the juices run.
  2. Meanwhile, cook the onions in the olive oil over the lowest heat you can manage. Stir now and then. They should take at least half an hour and turn the color of toffee.
  3. Squeeze the roasted garlic from its skins into the pot, add the tomatoes with all their juices, the paprika, and the stock.
  4. Simmer for fifteen minutes, then blend until completely smooth. Taste, season, and finish with the cream if you are using it.
  5. MARKER_METHOD_LAST Serve with bread you would happily eat on its own.
